story_theme_en: Lin created a survey about favorite fruits among her 25 classmates. Results: Orange 5 students, Strawberry 10 students, Banana 5 students, Grape 5 students. Lin needed to make a pictograph where each picture = 5 students.
helper_tip_en: Have students count symbols in each row and multiply by the symbol value shown in the key.
think_story_en: Pictograph: Strawberry 10 = 2 symbols (2x5=10) | Orange 5 = 1 | Banana 5 = 1 | Grape 5 = 1 | Total = 25 students. Strawberry is most popular.

data.content_en: Lin created a survey about favorite fruits among her 25 classmates. Results: Orange 5 students, Strawberry 10 students, Banana 5 students, Grape 5 students. Lin needed to make a pictograph where each picture = 5 students.

visual_blocks.content: Strawberry: 2x5=10 | Orange: 1x5=5 | Banana: 1x5=5 | Grape: 1x5=5 | Total = 25. Strawberry most popular.

visual_blocks.title: Pictograph
visual_blocks.description: A pictograph showing fruit preferences, 1 symbol = 5 students

visual_blocks.title: Try It!
visual_blocks.question: From the pictograph, which fruit do students like most and how many?
visual_blocks.explanation: Strawberry: 2 symbols x 5 = 10 students, the most.

data.question: From the pictograph, which fruit do students like most and how many?
data.explanation: Strawberry: 2 symbols x 5 = 10 students, the most.

explanation_steps_en: A pictograph uses pictures to represent data. Each picture has the same value.
Before reading a pictograph, check the key to find what 1 picture equals.
Count the pictures in each row, then multiply by the value of each picture.
A bar chart uses bars to represent data. Read the height or length of each bar.
To summarize data: find the highest value, lowest value, and total.

worked_examples_en.question_en: If 1 picture = 10 students and there are 3 pictures of oranges, how many students like oranges?

common_mistakes_en: Forgetting to check the key and multiplying by the wrong value.
Counting half a symbol as a full one.
Mixing up the X-axis and Y-axis on a bar chart.
hints_en: Always read the key first: 1 picture = ? students.
Count pictures one row at a time and multiply by the symbol value.
Check by adding all categories to see if they match the total.
